## How to read this list

`responsibilities` is verification-gated: only `{text: ..., verified: true}` is applicant experience, and `needs_verification` is excluded from every generated document (Master CV, tailored CV, cover letter, package text and email). A role title, a skill, a certificate, or the sector's normal practice is **not** evidence that a duty was performed — that is why these lines are still held after the applicant's own CV evidence was fully recovered.

| Action | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **CONFIRM** | The draft asserts nothing beyond the role you already record. Confirming it needs nothing more than your own attestation. The wording must still be yours: no draft here is paste-eligible. |
| **EDIT** | Part of the draft is already applicant evidence (and already restored as a verified responsibility); the wording above is the remainder. Keep it only if you personally did it, and author the wording yourself. |
| **DISCARD** | The draft's claim is named by no supplied fact and no verified item anywhere in the record. Recommend rejecting it unless you personally did exactly that. |

## What happens next (not performed by this tool)

1. Decide each line: CONFIRM (it is your experience), EDIT (keep the substance in your own words), or DISCARD (reject the inference).
2. `profile.yaml` changes only when you make them. A confirmed line becomes applicant experience only when you move `{text: <your wording>, verified: true}` into that role's `responsibilities`; discarded lines can be deleted from `needs_verification` in the same edit.
3. Check any candidate wording before you record it: `python tools/export_responsibility_review.py --verify-wording "your wording"` (read-only).
4. Re-run the suite: `python -m pytest -q`.

_This list is a presentation of the canonical record. It does not modify `profile.yaml`, it does not merge or release anything, and it does not apply a decision on your behalf._
